extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers / study section members (grant reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH definitions and guidance for critiquing Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (mechanisms R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), describing overall impact, core review criteria, and additional considerations reviewers should evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: likelihood to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s). R15: overall impact/priority score to reflect likelihood to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the institutional research environment. Consideration should be in light of the specific review criteria and any additional criteria applicable to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail or discussion. Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification may be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of the R15 program are to (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, and (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students in such environments to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 applications but may be included if available. Reviewers should consider the program objectives—strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research—when assessing impact and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies that have the potential for significant impact on biomedical or biobehavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An R21 need not have extensive background or preliminary information. Reviewers will focus evaluation on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to significantly advance knowledge or understanding. Appropriate justification can be via literature, other-source data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning Grant) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant Program (R34) supports development of Phase III clinical trials including establishing the team, developing data management/oversight tools, defining recruitment strategies, finalizing protocol, and preparing an operations manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The R34 is not designed for collection of preliminary data or conduct of pilot studies to support rationale. Reviewers should focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will successful completion change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 variant: additionally consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will substantially strengthen the school/academic component and expose students to research. Assess importance of the problem and potential to change the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage or New Investigators, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, evaluate whether investigators have complementary and integrated expertise and whether leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure are appropriate. R15 variant: also consider whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broader sense, or whether the proposal is a refinement, improvement, or new application of existing concepts or technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early-stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage particularly risky aspects? If the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, assess plans for: (1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and (2) justification for inclusion/exclusion based on sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children in terms of scientific goals and research strategy. R15 variant: similar wording; also consider whether the application provides sufficient evidence the project can stimulate student interest in biomedical/behavioral sciences careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources adequate for the proposed project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the project will benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements. R15 variant: assess availability of well-qualified students to participate and evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving human subjects (non-exempt), the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For research meeting exemption categories, evaluate: (1) justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials. See Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as inclusion (or exclusion) of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether inclusion/exclusion is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy. See Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five points: (1) proposed use of the animals, species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers; (2) justifications for use and appropriateness of species/numbers; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury, including use of analgesic/anesthetic/tranquilizing drugs or comfortable restraining devices; and (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. See the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards are present, determine whether adequate protection (biosafety/biocontainment) is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior critiques and whether revisions address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate productivity, accomplishments, and whether the proposed renewal builds on demonstrated progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision relates to a specific line of investigation from the original application that was not recommended, the committee will consider whether responses to prior comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether such opportunities either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in this section of the application regarding Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key assessment points: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession, use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three types called out: (1) Data Sharing Plan, (2) Sharing Model Organisms, and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan. Reviewers assess reasonableness of the plans or the rationale for not sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Sharing Plan (as part of Resource Sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Resource Sharing Plans rubric: reviewers comment on whether the Data Sharing Plan, or the rationale for not sharing, is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the adequacy and reasonableness of proposed data sharing arrangements relative to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing Model Organisms (as part of Resource Sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Resource Sharing Plans rubric: reviewers comment on whether the plan for sharing model organisms, or the rationale for not sharing, is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether plans for distribution and sharing of model organisms are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: GWAS / Genomic Data Sharing Plan (as part of Resource Sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Resource Sharing Plans rubric: reviewers comment on whether the GWAS/Genomic Data Sharing Plan, or the rationale for not sharing, is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate genomic data sharing approaches (e.g., consent, de-identification, repositories) and the reasonableness of proposed plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether requested funds and duration align with the scope and needs of the project; determine if any elements appear excessive or insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to offer constructive suggestions, point out major weaknesses, or advise on the need for substantial changes before resubmission.
